To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the quality of the governance mechanisms, based on market values, has a significant negative impact on the decision of the overvalued firms to issue a profit warnings.

the decision to issue an over-valuation profit warning is negatively affected by the use of performance-based compensation, by the presence of a majority of independent directors on the board, and by the existence of a compensation committee.

the quality of governance is not a significant factor explaining the decision of the management team to issue a PW, but that the market-based governance mechanisms have a negative influence on the decision to issue such a profit warning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the governance mechanisms of the firm, the decision to issue PW, and the impact of the PW on the market value of the firm.

the role played by the board in the decision to warn investors when the firm is not doing as well as expected, and it is also concerned with the role of market-based governance mechanisms in this same decision.
the decision of the board to disclose information about the firm's future performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of a company's governance has an impact on the decision to issue profit warnings, but this effect is not as significant as expected.

the governance characteristics of a firm do have an impact on its decision to issue profit warning, but this impact seems to be less significant than the impact of other characteristics such as the firm's size, the level of its leverage, and the quality of its accounting information.

the governance characteristics that have a positive impact on the decision to issue the profit warning when the company is overvalued are the following: the presence of a majority of outside directors, a higher proportion of outside directors, the presence of independent directors on the audit committee and a higher proportion of independent directors on this committee, the presence of a lead director and the presence of an audit committee.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

governance mechanisms based on ownership structures are more important than governance mechanisms based on the board of directors when a company is overvalued, and that the board of directors plays a role in the profit warning decision when the firm is under-valued.
the governance mechanisms based solely on the market value of equity do not appear to be the best way to align the interests of the shareholders with those of the managers.
the governance mechanisms based solely on the market values of the company seem to be more efficient than the mechanisms based on the characteristics of the board of directors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, contrary to what is generally believed, a good corporate governance does not always lead to a better decision making process.
the decision to issue profit warnings, which are often viewed negatively by the market, should be considered as a way for the management to signal its intention to improve its governance.
governance mechanisms are not the main determinants of the PW decision when a company is overvalued, but they do play an important role in the decision when it is not.
